# Lessons

## bug

### A 'last line is the max' shortcut only holds while a file has exactly one writer; merge=union silently gives it two

**Rule.** Any O(1) summary read from an append-only file's tail (clock, counter, high-water mark) is valid only under a single-writer invariant. If the file is ever combined by merge=union, sync, or copy from another clone, that invariant is gone and nothing on disk records it: derive the summary from the whole (cached) content, and make identities that name a writer unique per clone, not just per host and directory.

**Seen in:** B28589b8b26

### Never let 0 (or "") mean both 'unset' and a real value: use None for unset

**Rule.** When a numeric or string option has a default, represent 'not given' as None on every surface (argparse default=None, MCP a.get(k) is None) and validate the explicit value; `x or DEFAULT` silently turns an explicit 0/'' into the default, and in a safety tool that flips the answer in the unsafe direction.

**Seen in:** B22-minzero

## ddflow

### With parallel agents, never file a task under the 'next' sequential id: check it is free, or use a descriptive id

**Rule.** Several agents file B-numbers concurrently and task add overwrites an existing id without error, so 'the next free number' guessed from one agent's view clobbers another agent's item (even a running one). Before task add, confirm the id is unused (`ddflow show <id>` must fail), and prefer a descriptive id (B-json-failures) that no other agent will pick.

**Why.** 2026-09-28: my B205-B208 overwrote four other agents' items, one claimed and mid-pipeline; nothing warned.

**How to apply.** for id in ...; do ddflow show $id >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo TAKEN; done before filing; restore a clobbered item by re-adding its prior task.added fields from the event log.

**Seen in:** B16042585f4

## docsync

### git grep -o undercounts with many -F patterns: re-match whole lines instead

**Rule.** To learn WHICH of many fixed-string patterns occur, run git grep without -o and re-match the returned lines in Python

**Why.** B17 research: git grep --cached -o -h -w -F with ~190 -e patterns reported agent_id 19 times while -c showed it in many files, so live identifiers looked deleted

**How to apply.** git grep -h -w -F -e ... (whole lines), then set(regex.findall(lines))

**Seen in:** B17

## gates

### A gate command is read from the primary checkout but runs with the item branch's dependencies: merge main before unit_tests after the gate config changes

**Rule.** Before running the unit_tests gate, merge the base branch into the item branch whenever main changed .ddflow/config.toml's gate commands or the dev dependencies (e.g. the pytest-xdist '-n 48' change, 8fe68e6).

**Why.** load_gates reads the primary .ddflow/config.toml, but the command executes in the item's worktree with that branch's pyproject.toml/uv.lock; a branch cut before pytest-xdist was added fails with 'unrecognized arguments: -n 48'.

**How to apply.** git merge main in the item worktree (uv run then syncs the new dev deps), rerun the gate.

**Seen in:** B-parallel-tests

## ids

### With several agents on one queue, file items under descriptive ids (B-<slug>), never the next free number

**Rule.** Before 'task add', pick an id derived from the work (B-add-refuses-dup-id, BUG-companions), not max(B<n>)+1, and 'ddflow show <id>' first

**Why.** Until add refuses an existing id, a second 'task add B207' overwrote a running item's title/globs; three agents each picked 'the next number' within minutes (B205-B208 collided twice), and one agent's lease and gate records ended up under another agent's title, where complete would have counted them

**How to apply.** Descriptive ids cannot collide by accident; if a numbered id is required, re-read 'ddflow status' immediately before adding. After a collision: void the stray gate records with a reason, release, re-file under a new id, remove the duplicates

**Seen in:** 2026-09-28 B207/B208 overwritten (bugs B16042585f4, B6bd279367e)
